feedback: No race has been run yet, so there is no outcome for this geometry and none is claimed here. The geometry is a reasonable prior. Its five-sensor span (0.08 m) is about three times the 0.025 m tape, so the line should stay in view through moderate offsets. The 0.03 m forward offset gives the controller a look-ahead, but it also adds phase lag, so the controller needs derivative damping. For the first race, I am holding the geometry unchanged to get a clean baseline. Next steps depend on the telemetry. If steering_oscillation or max_error is high on the slalom or s-bend, the array is probably too wide or too far forward for the tight bends. In that case, try a narrower array (about 0.03 m total span, with x values at -0.015, -0.005, 0.005, 0.015 or similar) so fewer sensors are off-tape at once. If completion is poor because the robot is too slow or leaves the track, try a longer wheel_track or a smaller body_length to reduce yaw inertia. If line_loss_events is high, the array may be too narrow or the sensors too small for the 25 mm tape, so a larger sensor_size (0.016) could help.
requested_changes: Keep the current geometry for the first race to measure the baseline. Do not change it before telemetry is available.
If steering_oscillation or max_error is high on tight bends after the first race, narrow the sensor span to about 0.03 m total (x = -0.015 to +0.015) and keep the forward offset at y = 0.03.
If line_loss_events is high, try sensor_size 0.016 with the current spacing to make the line more visible to the outer sensors.
